newsitem.title: USA: Salomon Bros December same-store sales index up.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Bros December same-store sales index up.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said its same-store sales growth index registered a 6.2 percent gain in December, compared with a 1.8 percent rise a year ago.
In November, the index gained 3.9 percent.

"However, because of a significant shift in the calendar, we believe that the important Christmas selling season should be analyzed on a combined two-month (November-December) basis," Salomon retail analysts said in a report.
In general, the analysts said, December sales varied significantly by subsector and by company.

"On balance, however, we believe that sales were modestly below expectation for the month," the analysts said. "Despite a strong final week before Christmas, retailers were unable to make up for the five fewer shopping days between the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays this year."

Salomon analysts said they believe that the recent underperformance of retail stocks in general -- versus the overall market -- provides opportunities in select growth- and value-oriented retail equities, given their favorable risk/reward ratios.
